**Needs changes before merge.** One item blocks the merge. This is a SAFETY-tier review: the PR changes the machine travel check.

## What looks good

- The sweep math in `move_extremes` is the same reading as `cl::plane::sweep` (`crates/cl/src/cl/plane.rs:167`): the same frame, the same angles, the same larger radius. The check and the post read one arc the same way in XY, XZ and YZ.
- A zero sweep and a sweep that is not finite keep all four quarter points.
- The tests refuse the long way round, the swept side in two planes, a full circle and a quarter point on an endpoint.
- The PR changes no golden file, no snapshot PNG, no dependency and no process file. The decision record is present.
- The body has the `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #2710`. No UI file changed, thus no screenshots are necessary.

## Results (built locally, head `361c74c8d`, which contains `upstream/main` `75e74a9cb`)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: app build | ok |
| app lib | 380 passed, 1 ignored |
| `fourth_axis_pose` | 9 passed |
| `machine_arc_sweep` | 8 passed |
| `vmc_stroke` 5, `machine` 33, `lathe_stroke` 10, `lathe_thread_travel` 2, `plasma_machine` 6, `waterjet_machine` 13, `edm_machine` 5 | all passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Mutations that I ran again (each one restored afterwards):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `judge.rs` from `upstream/main` | red: 4 tests fail (the shallow arc, the two side tests, the no-sweep arc) |
| Ignore `arc.ccw` (the two `if arc.ccw` lines read `if true`) | red: 3 tests fail (the long way round, the two side tests) |

The two results agree with the table in the PR body. No golden file moved, thus there was none to read.

## Requested before merge

1. **`crates/app/src/machine/judge.rs:54` - `SAME_WORD` is smaller than the coarsest posted word.**
   The guard at line 41 keeps all four quarter points when the two endpoints can post as one point. Its bound is 0.001 mm. The comment at line 52 gives the finest word that a post writes. The guard needs the coarsest word.
   `crates/motion/src/ring_zig.rs:21-28` states that bound: a four-decimal inch post writes 2.54 um for each axis, and two endpoints less than `sqrt(2) * 0.00254` = 0.0036 mm apart can round to one point. On a diagonal, a three-decimal mm post rounds endpoints up to 0.0014 mm apart to one point.
   The post scripts write such an arc with equal endpoint words, and a control turns it a full circle. The new check judges only its two endpoints.

   I measured two arcs with a local test (not pushed), on the mill of `machine_arc_sweep.rs` (X -3000..3000):

   | Arc (G3, the short way) | Posted words | `upstream/main` | This PR |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `[2994.9995, -10, 0]` to `[2995.0015, -10, 0]`, center `(2995.0005, 0)`, chord 0.002 mm | four-decimal inch: `X117.9134 Y-0.3937` for the two ends | refused (X 3005) | `problems: []` |
   | `[2999.0706, -7.0714, 0]` to `[2999.0714, -7.0706, 0]`, center `(2992, 0)`, chord 0.00113 mm | three-decimal mm: `X2999.071 Y-7.071` for the two ends | refused (the old code adds X 3002) | `problems: []` |

   On the control, each arc is a full circle that goes past X 3000. The check on `upstream/main` refuses the two arcs. This PR passes them. That is a travel violation that passes silently (Prime Directive).

   The fix: make `SAME_WORD` not smaller than 0.0036 mm. `ring_zig::MIN_ARC_CHORD` uses 0.01 mm for the same law, with margin; the same value is a good choice here. Correct the comment at lines 52-53. Add a test with a chord between 0.001 mm and 0.0036 mm (the first row of the table is sufficient). Correct the decision record and the PR body, which give 0.001 mm.
   The cost is small: an arc with a chord below 0.01 mm keeps the old reading with four quarter points.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- `crates/app/tests/machine_arc_sweep.rs:12`: the Gate map names `cl::moves, cl::plane`. The suite tests `app::machine`; the two `cl` names make each `cl` change select this suite. This is your decision.
- The test at `machine_arc_sweep.rs:118` uses a chord of 0.4 um. After the fix, a second fixture near the new bound pins the bound itself.
- The PR body says that the reporter's project was not exercised. The reporter attached it to #2710 after the claim. A run of that project is good evidence, if it is easy to do.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: The endpoint guard was smaller than the coarsest posted word.

- Set `SAME_WORD` to 0.01 mm. Corrected the code comment, decision record, and PR body.
- Added `endpoints_that_round_to_one_inch_point_keep_all_four_quarter_points` with the review's 0.002 mm chord.
- The test passes at 0.01 mm. Reverting only the bound to 0.001 mm fails with `MachineCheck { problems: [] }`.
- Restoring 0.01 mm passes again.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passes all four steps.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
New head: `1a9f0f7425492f3edc733f6b5822321beac18ba0`.

Please review the new head again.

Ready for the maintainer to merge. No blocking findings.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The PR changes the machine travel check.

The previous finding is resolved:

- `crates/app/src/machine/judge.rs:55` sets `SAME_WORD` to 0.01 mm. The comment explains the four-decimal inch bound and the margin.
- `endpoints_that_round_to_one_inch_point_keep_all_four_quarter_points` pins the 0.002 mm chord from the previous review.
- The decision record and the PR body state the corrected bound.

The sweep uses the arc plane and direction. Full circles, equal posted endpoints, and zero sweeps keep all four quarter points. The radius uses the larger endpoint radius.

I built and tested locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-2712`. The trial merge with upstream main `3e615d653b934a7cd32091e81092b3cebf36efb5` succeeded. No GitHub runner was used.

| Check | Result |

| App library | 380 passed, 1 ignored |
| `fourth_axis_pose` | 9 passed |
| `machine_arc_sweep` | 9 passed |

| `lathe_stroke` | 10 passed |

| `waterjet_machine` | 13 passed |
| `edm_machine` | 5 passed |

I ran these temporary mutations locally:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Restore `judge.rs` from the tested upstream main | Red: 4 arc tests failed |
| Ignore `arc.ccw` in both angle calculations | Red: 3 arc tests failed |
| Restore only `SAME_WORD = 0.001` | Red: the inch-rounding test failed |
| Restore the reviewed source | Green: all 9 arc tests passed |

The worktree source is restored. No mutation or evidence was committed to the PR branch.

No golden file moved. No UI file changed, so before/after screenshots are not required. The PR adds no dependency and changes no process file. The decision record and the `Changelog:` and `Fixes #2710` lines are present.

Requested before merge: none.

Limits: I did not run the reporter's project or a full contour generate-and-post run. The local fixtures and the existing machine suites provide the test evidence above.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Merge class: SAME. The head is `1a9f0f7425492f3edc733f6b5822321beac18ba0`, the head that the review of 09:20 UTC names. No commit came after that review. The PR merges cleanly with `main`. This merge relies on that review by the review agent of a collaborator. The PR fixes a P3 issue (#2710), so no second review is necessary.
